subject: Targeted region degradation — interregional fallthrough routing & customer action items
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, John Lee <john.lee@fintech.co>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Targeted region degradation — brief notice and immediate steering guidance

Hello John / Acme ops team,

We detected sustained request errors and elevated token latency starting ~07:45 PDT in the us-east1 region that are impacting a subset of your inference traffic. Our control plane automatically enabled the configured fallthrough to eu-west while we investigate. You may see increased 99th percentile latency for requests routed cross-region.

Immediate notes and asks:
- We have not observed data residency changes or data exfiltration; logs show successful fallback routing and request processing in eu-west and asia-south.
- If you require traffic to remain in-region, please let us know immediately; otherwise our recommended temporary action is to accept the automatic fallthrough while we remediate.
- Please run the attached lightweight verification (customer-verification-checklist.csv) and share the results to confirm end-to-end behavior from your side.

What we are doing now:
- Ops team is running a targeted capacity reallocation and health checks in us-east1; failover remains active until explicit clearance.
- We will reduce cache TTLs for affected routes to 30s to avoid stale KV contexts during reroute.
- Estimated time to first mitigation update: 90 minutes. We will post interim updates to the Drive link below.

Attachments: impact_summary_20260829.pdf (short summary), customer-verification-checklist.csv
Runbook: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/regional-fallback

I will keep you updated directly. If you prefer a quick call for the next steps, I can connect Ops and our Infra team (Vanessa / David).

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: John Lee <john.lee@fintech.co>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 08:47:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted region degradation — brief notice and immediate steering guidance

Naomi — thanks for the heads up. Priority for us is correctness over speed; we can't accept traffic leaving the US for any PII-affecting endpoints. A few questions: 

1) Are customer session tokens or logs stored outside region during fallback?
2) What's the estimated window before full restoration in us-east?
3) Can you provide a short verification curl we can run from our infra to validate that requests land in eu/asia (if fallback continues)?

We are standing by; please loop in Security if there is any risk to data residency.

—John
John Lee
Platform Ops, FinTech Co (Acme Corp procurement)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:10:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Targeted region degradation — proposed mitigation steps

Naomi / team — internal ops plan below (I will own execution):

1) Keep automatic fallthrough enabled (eu-west / asia-south) for 30m while we run health checks.
2) Reduce inference cache TTL to 30s for affected customer routes and add a short-lived header to force KV refresh.
3) Start a rolling restart on the us-east gateway pods only; avoid restarting worker pools until we validate gateway health.
4) If customer requires strict in-region processing, we will open a scoped routing exception and migrate a spared pool in us-east to the customer's reserved capacity (requires approval, estimated 2–4 hrs).
5) Broadcast an interim notice to all impacted customers in the region with exact timing and CV checklist (Naomi — I can draft).

Attachments: regional-fallback-runbook.md

I'll capture timestamps and relevant kube logs for the post-incident packet. David — please pull the last 2 hours of LB traces and upload to the Drive folder so we can correlate.

Vanessa
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-corp.com, John Lee <john.lee@fintech.co>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Targeted region degradation — interregional fallthrough routing & customer action items

John / Acme ops — thank you, quick answers and an actionable checklist below.

Short answers:
- Data residency: No PII or session logs were written to external long-term stores during the fallthrough; ephemeral processing occurred in eu-west/asia-south while fallback was active. We will include the LB traces and a signed attestation in the post-incident packet.
- ETA for primary region restoration: initial fix attempt is in-progress; we expect a rolling gateway stabilization in 2–3 hours, with a potential full restoration in 4–6 hours depending on behavior. If you require immediate in-region processing, we can migrate a reserved pool (2–4 hours) — confirm and we will escalate.

Customer verification checklist (please run and paste results):
1) Run synthetic request against your standard endpoint and capture x-region header:
   curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1}'
   Look for our X-Region header (e.g., X-Redwood-Region: eu-west1) and X-Request-ID.

2) Report latency (p50/p95) and whether you see increased error 5xx rates.

3) If you run a regional-only policy, try to hit your in-region pinned endpoint (we can provide a per-customer pinned DNS entry on request).

Planned communications and next steps:
- We will keep fallthrough active until us-east health is green for 30 consecutive minutes.
- I will send hourly updates to this thread and a final post-incident packet once logs and traces are compiled.
- Action items for Acme: run the checklist, indicate whether you authorize temporary migration to a reserved pool, and confirm if you want an emergency SLA credit request pre-approved.

Attachments: impact_summary_20260829.pdf (summary), customer-verification-checklist.csv
Drive evidence: https://drive.redwood.com/AcmeCorp/incident-evidence-20260829

If helpful, I'll schedule a 15-minute bridge with Vanessa and David for a live verification run.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident follow-up & artifacts request — interregional fallthrough on 2026-08-29

Team — closing notes and next steps for the postmortem (we'll invite Product and Security):

Summary: the incident began 2026-08-29 14:45 UTC with a gateway health regression in us-east that triggered our fallthrough to eu-west/asia-south. Customer-facing mitigation (fallthrough) preserved request completion but produced cross-region latency for impacted tenants.

Requested artifacts (please upload to https://drive.redwood.com/AcmeCorp/incident-evidence-20260829 by EOD tomorrow):
- David: LB traces and the filtered 5xx logs for impacted routes (CSV + small sample logs).
- Soojin: kube events and gateway pod logs with timestamps (include restart reasons).
- Vanessa: exact timeline of actions taken and decision points (minutes precision).
- Ops: a short note about the TTL change and whether any cache invalidations were forced.

Agenda for the postmortem meeting (30–45m):
- Incident timeline and root-cause hypotheses
- Customer impact and verification artifacts
- Short-term fixes (runbook updates) and long-term mitigations (capacity / gateway hardening)
- Communications and SLA/credit discussion

I'll draft the public-facing post-incident email once we confirm artifacts; please add any additional required items to the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
